answer: Stake-weighted identity: each new agent must lock a deposit (its anchor) in a shared harbor contract before its votes count, and dishonest grading slashes that deposit. An attacker spinning up 1,000 fake identities must lock 1,000 deposits and loses them when caught colluding, so Sybil cost scales linearly with the number of fakes. Like an opal whose value comes from scarcity, influence comes from capital at risk, not from cheap keypairs.
